done_when: Approving a candidate-backed memory review saves the memory; the review card reports the real outcome (approved, failed with reason, or already decided); a Postgres test covers approving a candidate-backed review end to end

findings.body: The new Postgres tests exercise real persistence, but `click()` directly invokes a captured callback and manually connects the handlers. They never start the application or drive the required browser flow through Playwright. This bypasses production dispatch (`apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/channel-message-action-router.ts:100`), so the tests could pass even if deployed approval clicks never reach the executor. Add the required running-application test with real Postgres, verifying saved memory and visible approved, failed-with-reason, and already-decided outcomes; fake only third-party edges.
findings.title: Not done: End-to-end approval and review-card outcomes through the running application

why: Approving a learned memory always fails as stale while the card still says 'Memory review approved', so preferences and corrections can never be approved
